newsitem.title: USA: Texaco LA hydrotreater exploded - local radio.
newsitem.headline: Texaco LA hydrotreater exploded - local radio.

text.p: A hydrotreater at Texaco Inc's 64,000 barrel per day Wilmington oil refinery in the Los Angeles area exploded into flames early Monday morning, according to local radio station KFWB News.
The radio station said the shock of the initial explosion could be felt for blocks around the facility, and that over 100 firefighters were at the scene fighting the blaze.
A hydrotreater pulls sulphur out of diesel and other distillates to prepare the fuels for sale in the California markets, which has some of the strictest environmental specifications in the world.
It was not immediately clear if anyone was injured in the blast or if the fire was still burning.
But Brian Humphreys, a spokesman for the Los Angeles Fire Department, said there were no reports of deaths or injuries.
The refinery also has 32,300 barrels per day of catalytic cracking capacity, according to the National Petroleum Refining Association.
A catalytic cracker turns lighter feedstocks like residual fuel or diesel into light-end, high-profit fuels like gasoline.
